topic: Fracture clinic standards and virtual fracture clinic
usual_baseline: Face-to-face clinics miss the 72-hour standard: mean wait 10.7 days with 6% seen in time [1318]. Where a VFC already runs, referral is high but not complete: 88.0% [1393], 96% [1375]. Before VFC triage, only 39% were triaged within 24 hours [1478]. ED referral errors were 32.1% [1563].
fix_that_works: A virtual fracture clinic for all ED referrals: 100% reviewed within 72 hours, mean 1.3 days [1318]. Mandatory VFC triage with patient-initiated follow-up: 100% within 24 hours, face-to-face visits down 50.2% [1478]. Senior approval before face-to-face: 96% to 99% [1375]. ED teaching, posters and a leaflet: 88.0% to 98.4% [1393]. ED referral guidelines: errors 32.1% to 12.6% [1563].
fix_that_fails: Rota changes, more doctors and extra seating in a face-to-face clinic changed little: wait 3.55 to 3.21 days, overall experience excellent 50.72% to 53.55%; waiting area and X-ray ratings stayed poor [1330].
consultant_advice: Showing that a VFC meets the 72-hour standard is well done. The fix is known and works. More useful: audit what the VFC misses, such as GP and outside referrals [1375], and measure patient safety and satisfaction after virtual discharge, which none of these audits assessed [1478].
